1. Nat Neurosci. 2002 Jul;5(7):688-94. doi: 10.1038/nn871.

Morphology of Heschl's gyrus reflects enhanced activation in the auditory cortex 
of musicians.

Schneider P(1), Scherg M, Dosch HG, Specht HJ, Gutschalk A, Rupp A.

Author information:
(1)Department of Physics, University of Heidelberg, Philosophenweg 12, D-69120 
Heidelberg, Germany. Peter_Schneider@med.uni-heidelberg.de

Using magnetoencephalography (MEG), we compared the processing of sinusoidal 
tones in the auditory cortex of 12 non-musicians, 12 professional musicians and 
13 amateur musicians. We found neurophysiological and anatomical differences 
between groups. In professional musicians as compared to non-musicians, the 
activity evoked in primary auditory cortex 19-30 ms after stimulus onset was 
102% larger, and the gray matter volume of the anteromedial portion of Heschl's 
gyrus was 130% larger. Both quantities were highly correlated with musical 
aptitude, as measured by psychometric evaluation. These results indicate that 
both the morphology and neurophysiology of Heschl's gyrus have an essential 
impact on musical aptitude.

DOI: 10.1038/nn871
